title: Multiplex stream shim: Dual AsyncIterator / WebStream adapter for TS SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customers use both AsyncIterator and Web Streams across Node/Deno/Browser. We need a compact shim that exposes a single producer surface usable by both consumer styles, supports safe drain-and-swap handoffs, preserves backpressure and cancellation semantics, and provides diagnostic metrics. This work implements getDualStream(producer) which returns a dual-consumption object to simplify migrations and reduce duplicated producer code.
acceptance_criteria: A1: getDualStream(producer) implemented and exported from @redwood/ts-sdk/streams; returns object with asAsyncIterator() and asWebStream()
A2: Backpressure mapping validated: WebStream highWaterMark signals producer pause; iterator pacing bounds queue growth and metrics reflect stalls
A3: Drain-and-swap API implemented: dual.swapTo({type:'web'|'iterator'}, {timeoutMs}) that finishes without dropping partial tokens or loses ordering
A4: Cancellation propagation: controller.abort() triggers iterator.return(); iterator.return()/throw() triggers controller.close()/error() and original error is surfaced
A5: Unit and integration tests covering Node/Deno/browser-like environments plus stress test proving bounded memory for slow consumers
A6: Docs and migration snippet added to docs/ts-sdk/streaming.md and PR links provided in ticket
implementation_notes: Use a bounded ring buffer with lease tokens; producer awaits when buffer full via a pauseIfNeeded promise
First consumer call acquires exclusive mode by default; explicit shared mode via asAsyncIterator({mode:'shared'}) or asWebStream({mode:'shared'})
swapTo(target) will wait for in-flight buffer to drain then transfer lease; configurable timeout supports force-swap or abort
Map WebStream controller.queue size to producer backpressure; estimate bytes for items when available to cap buffer
Serialize finalization to avoid races when iterator.return() and controller.abort() occur concurrently
Emit telemetry shim.bufferedItems, shim.bufferedBytesEstimate, shim.drainLatencyMs under ts.sdk.stream.shim key
Keep implementation small (~200-350 LOC), zero runtime deps, exported via getDualStream helper and DualStream type only
testing_plan: Unit tests: ring buffer edge cases, lease arbitration, cancellation mapping, producer faster than consumer simulation
Integration: Node tests with web-streams-polyfill, Deno runner job, Playwright headless browser test for controller semantics
Stress: synthetic producer at ~10k small chunks/sec for 10s with variable consumer delays to validate bounded memory and stable latency
CI: add matrix jobs for node:18, node:20 and browser:chrome-headless
Benchmarks: measure median/p95 drain latency for swapTo under small/medium/large payloads and attach to PR
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag TS_SDK_DUAL_STREAM=beta and publish canary package
Collect telemetry for 2 weeks; monitor for OOMs or repeat errors and escalate to runtime team if needed
Publish migration guidance and examples in SDK docs and announce in SDK release notes
Enable by default in ts-sdk-2.6 if telemetry stable; backport fixes to 2.5 on customer request
